The Polar Vortex Is About to Make Weather Weird From the UK to the US

Wired November 12, 2026

A critical blockade against some of nature’s coldest air has temporarily broken down—and much earlier in the year than normal. Disruptions in this circulation, known as the polar vortex, often push intensely cold air out of the Arctic toward lower latitudes.

Experts still aren’t entirely sure how the current collapse will play out in our everyday weather. But it’s another sign that we may be in for a wild ride over the weeks and months to come.

The polar vortex is a band of upper-level winds wrapping around the Arctic Circle like a dam. This circulation is usually strong and stable, helping to keep the season’s coldest air locked near the North Pole. But the winds occasionally weaken or even reverse course, which can set off an atmospheric chain reaction, allowing bitterly cold air to spill southward.

The manner in which the polar vortex breaks down determines what kind of weather conditions we might expect. Upper-level winds dipping southward in troughs are responsible for brief spells of cold temperatures. These “lobes” of the polar vortex, as they’re known, are relatively common in a typical winter.

Sometimes, this circulation can splinter into smaller pieces. If the vortex were a flowing river, these fragments are like leaves stuck on the riverbank, forcing extremely cold air to linger over the same areas for days or weeks at a time.

One such case made this phenomenon a household name. A highly disrupted polar vortex in early 2015 sent a weeks-long burst of cold air sweeping over the eastern US. Chicago recorded its coldest February in nearly 140 years. In Lexington, Kentucky, temperatures bottomed out at –18 degrees Fahrenheit, as subfreezing air dove all the way to the Gulf of Mexico.

Seeing a breakdown of the polar vortex this early in the season is unprecedented in the historical record. Disruptions of this extent typically don’t occur until the latter half of winter. Based on the latest data, the circulation’s reversal began on Tuesday, and computer model guidance expects it to last through Thursday.

Weather patterns take a few weeks to respond to a polar vortex disruption, if at all. Given that reliable forecasts only extend about 10 days into the future, we can’t know where in the northern hemisphere cold air from the Arctic may spill.

While experts are still debating the exact causes driving this polar vortex breakdown, the event throws another wrench into a cool season already dominated by another unprecedented event: the strongest El Niño on record.

Historically warm sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific Ocean have already significantly affected conditions around the world, and this influence will only grow heading into the winter months.

Much of North America can expect warmer-than-normal conditions during a winter dominated by a strong El Niño. But every event is different, and now with a sudden disruption in the polar vortex, those forecasts are less certain, because unexpected things can happen when unprecedented phenomena overlap.

Well, Vitamix crushes the blender game, but it usually comes with a price tag to match. Luckily, Vitamix promo codes crop up at various points during the year, and we’re here to help you stay up to date on those discounts.

Vitmix’s top-of-the-line blender, Ascent X5, now features a stainless-steel container. The 48-ounce stainless-steel container is not only large and hygienic but also combines an intuitive touch interface with a refined, timeless design. The non-reactive stainless-steel material resists stains, odors, and corrosion, and it expertly handles hot, cold, and acidic ingredients. This futuristic gadget also has an automatic self-cleaning program and ten blending programs for popular items like smoothies, soups, frozen cocktails, and more, for a precise blend every time.

Vitamix offers many ways to save on these handy kitchen gear items, including $50 off when you register your email. All you have to do is enter your email on Vitamix’s website, and you’ll get a discount of up to $50 sent straight to your inbox. Plus, you’ll get free shipping on orders of $100 or more.

Vitamix

Amazon

Glad you asked. Vitamix is offering free standard shipping on orders over $99. This means ground shipping is free for blenders at the current discounts. However, priority shipping is not free.

WIRED has long sung the praises of the classic Vitamix 5200. The model converted contributing reviewer Joe Ray after he realized that the “model of preference for blender aficionados around the world” was also his key to home mole and Oaxacan-style cookery.

A similar road-to-Damascus moment struck WIRED contributing reviewer Heather Arndt Anderson when she tested the Vitamix Ascent X2, which is currently on a $50 promo discount. “The more I thought about it,” she wrote, “the more I realized that maybe I’ve never been a blender person because I never had a good blender.” Anderson also made a big batch of mole without passing out from chile fumes, then moved on to homemade masa and a Georgian walnut spread. She regretted only that the blender wasn't easier to clean.

After testing a number of brands' blenders, WIRED contributing reviewer Emily Peck marveled that even the basic Vitamix Explorian E310 churned almonds frictionlessly into butter without even needing a presoak.

Buying like-new refurbished Vitamix blenders and appliances is a great way to save hundreds of dollars and go green with less waste. Be sure to check out Vitamix refurbished blenders, as they’re constantly adding new refurbished appliances. Once they’re gone, they’re gone! Right now, a certified reconditioned Vitamix Propel 750 is only $230—a savings of $400! And a certified reconditioned Vitamix Venturist Pro is only $240—a savings of $310.

One of the reasons we on the gear team like Vitamix machines is because of their versatility. And Vitamix makes it extra easy to make the most of your Vitamix blender, with tons of Vitamix soup recipes, plus curry, sauces, and more. Make the most out of your device, whether its a Vitamix Professional Series 750 or 5200, Vitamix has the best recipes for you.

Take $200 Off the MacBook Air With This Early Black Friday Deal

Wired November 12, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

Well ahead of Black Friday, the MacBook Air is already $200 off, bringing down the price of the 13-inch model with an M5 chip, 16 GB of RAM, and 512 GB of storage to $1,099.

This is the lowest price the MacBook Air has been at since June, when Apple permanently hiked prices across its entire Mac lineup. Amazon frequently sells this MacBook Air for $1,149, but this even lower price is usually reserved for big sales events—the last being in October during Prime Day. And now it's back.

Apple

Amazon (13-inch)

Walmart (13-inch)

Apple (13-inch)

I probably don't need to expound too much on what makes the M5 MacBook Air such a fantastic, do-it-all laptop. It's extremely well-built, the performance and battery life are both top-notch, and it's still one of the thinnest laptops you can buy. There's a reason it tops my list of laptop recommendations—even after having tested dozens of new models this year.

Unlike the MacBook Neo, which makes compromises on memory and performance to achieve its low price, the MacBook Air does nearly everything right. And while a MacBook Pro may tempt you—whether the new M6 model or one of the more powerful touchscreen OLED models—most people won't actually feel the difference in performance. Unless content creation, media, or game development is a full-time gig for you, I think you'll be surprised by just how much the M5 MacBook Air can handle.

The only real question is what size is right for you. The 13-inch model plays to the strengths of the MacBook Air—offering an extremely portable laptop at a reasonable price without sacrificing performance. If you would appreciate a larger screen (and don’t plan to travel with the device as much), you might prefer the 15-inch model, which is also $200 off its retail price, currently selling for $1,299. Aside from the larger screen, the only other difference is a much more robust six-speaker audio system.

Either way, now remains a really good time to buy a MacBook Air. While prices were certainly lower in the first half of 2026, we’re still probably many months out from the inevitable M6 refresh. I don’t claim to have any insider knowledge, but based on pricing history, I can’t see these laptops coming down any lower in price over the next few months.

For more early Black Friday deals, make sure to check out the discounts we've been watching on some of our favorite products.

Wired November 12, 2026

All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.

Black Friday isn’t officially here until November 27, but plenty of early deals are already live. Several walking pads are currently marked down, and with winter coming, right now is the ideal time to make use of the discount. I, for one, have already started prepping my hibernation cave by stocking happy lights, arts and crafts, and a brand-new walking pad.

By the time Black Friday arrives, stepping outside might feel like taking a cold plunge. At that point, you’ll wish you had snagged a walking pad sooner to help you reach your step count goals without risking frostbite. Below, get a curated list of walking pad treadmills I have tested and vetted that are on sale.

Urevo

Shop

Amazon

Urevo

Shop

Urevo

The Urevo CyberPad is my favorite walking pad, and it’s on sale for $390 ($110 off). I’m confident in the product’s durability, mainly due to its sturdy-feeling build and comfortable belt. It offers a 14-percent incline, which is one of the highest available in walking pads, and the speed tops out at 4 mph. Unfortunately, the incline capability makes the machine difficult to store under furniture. It weighs about 71 pounds, so moving it around isn’t fun, but the wheels help. You can control the CyberPad with its remote control and companion app. You can also view your real-time metrics on the machine’s display.

The Urevo Strol 2S Pro is also on sale for $210 off. This 2-in-1 doubles as a treadmill with adjustable handrails, a display, and an attachable tablet holder. It was simple to set up, complete with a remote control and intuitive companion app. It feels super stable underfoot, even at top speed and incline level (7.6 mph and 9 percent). That top speed likely isn’t fast enough if you’re looking to sprint, but it’s plenty for a good workout. The machine is unobtrusive, has a quiet motor, and the 43-inch track is compact enough to place under your desk. Overall, it’s a sturdy walking pad treadmill that offers great value and range.

WalkingPad

Shop

Amazon

The WalkingPad C2 Foldable Walking Treadmill’s track is 32.5 inches when folded (and unfurls to 57 inches), making it a great option for storage in small spaces. It weighs 62 pounds, which isn’t light, but it makes for a sturdier running deck and a (hopefully) longer lifespan. You can adjust the speed via the remote control or companion app. Reviewer Kristin Canning found the app itself to be a little wonky. For example, if you don’t start a workout within the app, your data won’t sync. The app also saves each walking session separately, so if you take a break, you start from zero again. The good news is you don’t need to use the app in order to enjoy the walking pad.

Canning also didn’t like that when you first start using the machine, you have to walk at slower speeds before you can unlock the upper end of the range. This might appeal to folks who enjoy gamifying their workouts, though. The app also offers workout programs, which auto-adjust the speed to your pace via sensors under the belt.
